name: Heroes of Faith
big_question: What makes someone a hero of faith?

glossary.d: someone admired for their courage and for standing up for others
the teaching that no harm should be caused to any living thing
an Indian word meaning a spiritual community
believing some people are better than others because of skin colour
refusing to use force or harm to win a struggle
modest; not thinking you are more important than other people
living together peacefully, even when people are different
South African rule that kept Black and white people apart
treating a person worse because of who they are
fairness; making sure people get what is right
the belief that every person has the same worth and rights
keeping groups apart by law, such as in schools or buses
treating a group of people cruelly and unfairly for a long time
learning at school, which Malala says is a right for every girl
the belief that women and girls should have equal rights
doing what is right even when it is frightening or dangerous

lessons.title: Gandhi
lessons.big_question: Why is Gandhi remembered as a hero today?
aims: DESCRIBE — who Gandhi was and where he lived and worked
DISCUSS — what makes a person a hero
EXPLAIN — how ahimsa shaped Gandhi's response to racism

questions: What characteristics does a hero have? Give two.
Name a person you think is a hero. Say why.
Can an ordinary person be a hero? Explain your answer.

learn.caption: Gandhi: his life, his beliefs and his response

source.quote: In Gandhi's ashram people of different religions, races and backgrounds shared all their possessions, ate together and were involved in the struggle to live in harmony.
source.attrib: — Unit 5 lesson slides, on Gandhi's ashram
source.task: Underline what the people in the ashram shared. Explain how this answered the racism Gandhi saw.

stretch.question: Explain two teachings we learn from Gandhi.

debate.statement: Non-violence is always the best way to fight unfairness
agree: Gandhi followed ahimsa, causing no harm, and he still changed the way people were treated.
Violence usually makes enemies hate each other more, so the unfairness never really ends.
disagree: Some people in power ignore peaceful protest, so nothing changes and the suffering goes on.
Gandhi's work took many years, and people treated badly may not have that long to wait.
debate.how_to_win: Use the word ahimsa and give one real example from Gandhi's life to back up your point.

quickfire.q: Who was the first Guru of Sikhism?
Name two of the Five Ks.
What is a gurdwara?
What do Sikhs teach about nature?
What does Ahimsa mean?
How did Gandhi respond to racism?

lessons.title: Nelson Mandela
lessons.big_question: Why is Nelson Mandela remembered as a hero?
aims: DESCRIBE — what apartheid was in South Africa
DISCUSS — whether it is ever right to break a law
EXPLAIN — why Mandela is remembered as a hero

questions: Is it ever okay to break a law? Explain why or why not.
Name one law you think is fair. Say why it is fair.
What should people do if a law is unfair?

learn.caption: Apartheid, and how Mandela stood against it
rows: Apartheid: the state of being apart
Unfair treatment set down in law

source.quote: In the 1940s South Africa was under apartheid rule. This meant white people were treated as superior to Black people. Mandela believed everybody should be treated the same.
source.attrib: — Unit 5 lesson slides, on the apartheid rule
source.task: Underline what apartheid meant. Then write one sentence saying what Mandela believed instead.

stretch.question: Explain two reasons why Nelson Mandela is remembered as a hero.

debate.statement: Mandela being imprisoned was clearly the wrong decision
agree: He was asking for Black and white people to be treated the same, which is only fair.
In 1996 the United Nations called apartheid a crime against humanity.
disagree: He did break the law, and courts are meant to treat everyone who breaks a law the same.
Some would say he could have kept campaigning and stayed free to lead his people.
debate.how_to_win: Say what apartheid was before you give your opinion, and use the words justice and equality.

quickfire.q: What are the Five Ks in Sikhism?
Where do Sikhs go to worship?
What does Ahimsa mean?
What is an Ashram?
What does apartheid mean?
How long was Mandela in prison?

lessons.title: Martin Luther King
lessons.big_question: Why is Martin Luther King remembered as a hero?
aims: DESCRIBE — what segregation meant for Black Americans
DISCUSS — what King's dream for the future was
EXPLAIN — two ideas King used to fight segregation

questions: What is one dream you have for the world? Explain it.
Why do people need hope when life is unfair?
Name one thing you would change about the world today.

learn.caption: Segregation, and how King answered it
rows: The I Have a Dream speech
All made in the image of God

source.quote: I have a dream that my four little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the color of their skin but by the content of their character.
source.attrib: — Martin Luther King, I Have a Dream speech
source.task: Underline the words that say how King wants people to be judged. Explain what that means.

stretch.question: Explain two ideas Martin Luther King used to stop segregation.
starters: Firstly, we are all made in the image of God
Secondly, we must love our neighbours

debate.statement: A speech can do more to end racism than a law can
agree: King's I Have a Dream speech changed how millions of people thought about racism.
Laws can be ignored, but words like King's still give people hope today.
disagree: Segregation was written into law, so only a change in the law could truly end it.
Speeches can be forgotten, but a law protects people every single day.
debate.how_to_win: Quote one line from the speech, then say what a law can do that a speech cannot.

quickfire.q: Who was Guru Nanak?
How many Ks are in the Five Ks?
What was apartheid?
How long was Mandela imprisoned for?
What is segregation?
What famous speech did MLK give?

lessons.title: Malala Yousafzai
lessons.big_question: Why is Malala considered a hero by millions of people?
aims: DESCRIBE — what happened to Malala in 2008 and 2012
DISCUSS — why every girl should be able to go to school
EXPLAIN — two lessons we can learn from Malala

questions: Why is going to school important? Give two reasons.
Is education a right or a reward? Explain your answer.
What would you miss most if school were taken away?

learn.caption: Malala: her life, her courage and her fund

source.quote: I could live a quiet life or I could make the most of this new life I had been given. I chose to continue my fight until every girl could go to school.
source.attrib: — Malala Yousafzai, on her life after 2012
source.task: Underline the choice Malala made. Explain in one sentence why that choice took courage.

stretch.question: Explain two lessons we can learn from Malala.

debate.statement: Every girl should have twelve years of free education
agree: Malala says more than 130 million girls are out of school today, which is unfair on them.
Education helps people out of poverty, so teaching girls helps whole countries.
disagree: Some countries are too poor to build enough schools, so the promise could not be kept.
Some families need older children at home or at work, so twelve years may not suit all.
debate.how_to_win: Use one statistic from the lesson, then say who would have to pay for the schools.
